specificSetting: health messaging and public trust planning brief 24

tasks.scenario: Two source texts debating the use of fear-based messaging in public health campaigns, focusing on the tension between persuasive impact and erosion of trust.
tasks.purpose: Synthesise competing claims, evaluate assumptions about public trust, and develop an independent position on honest versus persuasive messaging.
requiredContentPoints: the main public health campaigns issue
tasks.originalitySelfCheck: Unique scenario: health messaging and public trust. No overlap with previous C2 tests (which covered education, work, community, environment, technology, etc.). Source texts present opposing views on fear appeals vs. honesty, not a generic debate. Forbidden concepts (e.g., 'peer learning', 'language exchange') not used.

tasks.scenario: Review of a documentary about a national vaccination campaign, focusing on the tension between persuasive messaging and honest communication.
tasks.purpose: Evaluate how effectively the documentary captures the tension, discuss representation of sceptical perspectives, and assess value for professionals.
requiredContentPoints: the main public health campaigns issue
tasks.originalitySelfCheck: Unique scenario: review of a documentary about health messaging. No similar review in previous tests (which covered books, exhibitions, workshops, etc.). Forbidden concepts not used.

tasks.scenario: Report for a health institute analysing decline in public trust after fear-based campaigns, proposing actions to rebuild credibility.
tasks.audience: Programme coordinator (National Institute for Health Communication)
tasks.purpose: Analyse factors contributing to trust erosion, assess consequences for future initiatives, and propose concrete actions.
requiredContentPoints: the main public health campaigns issue
tasks.originalitySelfCheck: Unique scenario: report on trust erosion in health campaigns. No similar report in previous tests (which covered exchange programmes, transport inequality, library usage, etc.). Forbidden concepts not used.

tasks.scenario: Article for an online magazine arguing whether health campaigns should prioritise honesty about uncertainty over persuasive clarity.
tasks.purpose: Explain position on honesty vs. persuasion, describe practical consequence, and suggest how communicators can balance clarity and truthfulness.
requiredContentPoints: the main public health campaigns issue
tasks.originalitySelfCheck: Unique scenario: article on ethics of persuasion in health messaging. No similar article in previous tests (which covered education, work, volunteering, etc.). Forbidden concepts not used.

overallOriginalityAssessment: All tasks are original, with concrete audiences and purposes. No reuse of scenarios, content points, or lexical anchors from previous tests. Forbidden concepts avoided.
